title: The Work Between Moments
logline: A skilled worker judges a raw material in about a second, commits to a cut that cannot be taken back, and works it to a finish that reality alone decides.
human_question: When a whole trade rests on judgements made faster than anyone can explain them, what is actually happening inside each of those moments?

situation.what_happens: A worker receives a piece of raw material that has to be read before anything can be done to it. The first judgement is made in about a second and decides what the piece will become, what it will be worth, and whether the day's labour is wasted; the worker cannot fully say how it was made. Then comes the working itself, a sequence of steps most of which cannot be undone, carrying dozens of smaller judgements of the same kind: a check, a correction, a pause, a decision to stop. At the end the piece is right or it is not, and the difference is money.
situation.who_is_involved: The worker whose judgement the trade actually pays for; whoever is learning the trade beside them and does not yet see what they see; the person who supplied the raw material and the person waiting for the finished piece, both of whom have money riding on a judgement neither of them can check.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the worker, the value of the piece and a reputation built entirely on being right quickly. For the learner, whether a skill its own holder cannot explain can be handed on at all. For the supplier and the buyer, real money. For the film, the obligation never to present a person's face as evidence of what is happening in their mind.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Work like this begins when a piece arrives and ends when it is finished, sold or spoiled, usually within a day or a few days. The pressures are the material itself, the light available to see it by, the time it takes and what has been promised to somebody else. It can end with a piece worth more than the material, a piece worth less, or a piece ruined by one wrong move, and which of those happens is decided by the material and the hand, not by the film.

concept_merge.why_together: C020 contributes the claim that every moment of experience, however small, carries the same seven parts: something touches the mind, it feels like something, it is recognised, there is a push behind the next move, the mind rests on one aspect of it, the moment is sustained, and attention is pointed. Its account of recognition is what this film is about: each act of recognising leaves a mark, the next recognises by that mark, and over time recognition becomes firm, which is why a craftsperson sees a flaw at a glance and cannot say how. C036 contributes the limit on what the eye actually receives, a blend of colour and never the thing itself, so the name, the grade and the price are added afterwards from everything seen before. C032 contributes the claim that no moment is ever flavourless: each one arrives pleasant, painful or neither, and the sources say there is no fourth way. In a trade built on instant judgement all three run inside a single second of work.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: On its own C020 is a list to be memorised. Set inside work where a judgement is worth money, it becomes an account of how a skill is actually built, not by insight but by years of marks laid down on top of one another, and it explains the thing skilled people always say, that they know but cannot tell you how. Adding C036 shows that the instant verdict is not a deeper kind of seeing but the same bare colour everyone gets, with a lifetime of naming attached to it. And because C032 insists every such moment has a tone, the film can hold the fact that one second was both a technical judgement and something that felt like something, including, as the digest notes, pain nobody knows about unless they ask.

concept_links.why: The digest gives the seven factors as present in every single mind without exception, contact, feeling, perception, volition, one-pointedness, the mental life-faculty and attention, and adds that in the weakest minds, the ten sense-consciousnesses, these seven are the only factors present [C020-P:L27-L29; C020-P:L111]. Its account of perception carries this film: recognising works by marks, each recognition leaves a mark for the next, recognition grows firm over time, and perception knows 'red' without knowing why it is red. Four of the digest's limits are held to. Attention here is not mindfulness in the modern sense: it is present in angry and greedy minds too and cannot by itself choose good over bad [C020-P:L109]. Volition as kamma is not 'intention is what counts'; the source ties it to every act, even eating or walking, and to results that follow like a debt [C020-P:L75-L79]. The life-faculty is not a soul or 'life energy', a misreading the digest warns against by name [C020-P:L97]. One-pointedness is not productivity focus; it is present even in a restless mind, which the source compares to a jolting chariot that still carries its passenger [C020-P:L89]. The seven are a way of attending to real work, never a seven-step structure for the film and never a diagnosis of anyone's mind.

Folded in with IDEA-0075. The digest insists the eye meets only colour, a blend of the colours of many tiny clusters, and that knowing 'I saw such-and-such a thing' comes from marks learned in earlier seeing [C036-P:L37-L41; C036-M:L9]. A trade in which a material's worth is settled by eye in about a second is that gap made economic: what arrives is colour, and the grade, the name and the price are added from experience. The digest's guard applies without exception: 'perception is an illusion' distorts the source, for which colour is a real event and only the assembled, named thing is a convention.

The digest states that feeling is present in every mind, that by the way it is experienced it is threefold, pleasant, painful or neutral, and that the sources say outright there is no fourth way [C032-M:L5; C032-P:L43]. That keeps the film from flattening a long, difficult working day into one mood. The digest also separates hidden pain, a toothache or a mind burning with worry that nobody knows about unless they ask, from the open kind, which is exactly why this film may never attribute a feeling from a face alone and must wait for the participant's own words. C032 belongs to another group's concept set and is carried here because this episode's lesson teaches it; nothing in this idea extends it past what that lesson cites.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: Every moment of real work, easy or hard, is made of the same few parts: something is touched, it feels a certain way, it is recognised, there is a push behind the next move, and attention points somewhere. A skilled worker's instant judgement is not a gift but thousands of earlier recognitions stacked on each other, which is why they are right and cannot tell you how.
what_must_be_real: The material, the money and the consequence must be real, and no judgement may be re-made for the camera. The edit may never offer a face alone as evidence of an inner state: comfort, pain, recognition and decision are described by the participant in their own words and never supplied by an interviewer. The seven factors are not to be narrated over the work as though they could be watched happening, which the digests say plainly they cannot.
position_hint: middle: a close study of ordinary skilled work, placed after the films about what a single sense receives and before the films about how a sequence too fast to watch is taught and charted. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Drifting into passive observation of a task with nothing genuinely at stake.
Over-attributing inner feeling to facial expression rather than to what a participant actually says.
Narrating the seven factors over the work as a checklist, which the digest's warnings about attention, volition and one-pointedness rule out.

Glamorising a trade whose product can be worth a great deal while the labour behind it is not, or exposing prices, sourcing or trade confidences that could put a participant at risk (folded in from IDEA-0075).
Treating an instant judgement as mystical skill rather than as accumulated recognition, which is what the sources actually describe.
drop_if: The work has no independent human stake beyond illustrating the concepts.
Access would require staging actions or disrupting a livelihood.
Participants do not want inner experience discussed, so the film could only infer it from images.
The judgements turn out to be freely revisable, so nothing is actually risked in the moment.
Research shows the framework distorts how the participants understand their own work.

connections.note: Takes in the instant-verdict strand: a material judged by eye in about a second, the years behind that second, and the gap between raw colour and a trained name and price.
Both are built from repeated small acts of noticing and response across an ordinary working day, one over a material and one over a street.
One watches colour judged fast in poor light with no time to check, the other a judgement that is checked and then made irreversible by a tool.

selection.reason: Carries EPD-0043, and is no longer an abstract 'any real task': IDEA-0075's instant-verdict situation and its C036 link give it a real trade to be about.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
C084 was read during the pilot phase and deliberately left unattached; this idea does not need it.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
